name: Sinus bradycardia
summary: A sinus rhythm at 45/min in this example. Rate alone does not establish the cause or clinical significance.

lessons.title: Slow regular ventricular rate
lessons.explanation: R–R intervals are about 1.33 seconds: 60,000 / 1,333 is approximately 45/min.

lessons.title: P before every QRS
lessons.explanation: An upright lead-II P wave precedes every narrow QRS with the same PR interval.

lessons.title: Interpret perfusion and context
lessons.explanation: This rhythm may be physiological or secondary to disease or medication. Assess symptoms, blood pressure and perfusion.

name: Sinus tachycardia
summary: Regular sinus activity at 120/min. Look for a physiological or pathological driver rather than diagnosing the cause from rate alone.

lessons.title: Regular 120/min rhythm
lessons.explanation: QRS complexes recur every 500 ms, corresponding to 120/min.

lessons.title: Consistent P–QRS relationship
lessons.explanation: P waves precede the QRS with a fixed PR. At faster rates P can approach the preceding T wave.

lessons.title: Narrow QRS
lessons.explanation: The modeled QRS is 90 ms. This example does not show a wide-complex tachycardia.

name: Atrial flutter · 2:1 conduction
summary: Continuous flutter activity at 300/min with a ventricular response of 150/min. A regular rate near 150 should prompt inspection for hidden flutter waves.

lessons.title: Continuous flutter activity
lessons.explanation: Negative sawtooth activity repeats every 200 ms in this lead-II teaching strip. There is no normal isoelectric P–P baseline.

lessons.title: Two atrial cycles per QRS
lessons.explanation: The atrial rate is twice the ventricular rate; one flutter wave can be obscured by QRS or T.

lessons.title: Regular ventricular response
lessons.explanation: QRS complexes recur every 400 ms: a ventricular rate of 150/min.

name: Regular narrow-complex SVT
summary: A regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 180/min. The strip illustrates SVT morphology without assigning an AVNRT or AVRT mechanism.

lessons.title: Fast regular QRS train
lessons.explanation: The R–R interval is approximately 333 ms, corresponding to 180/min.

lessons.title: Narrow complexes
lessons.explanation: The modeled QRS is 80 ms. QRS width and regularity help organize the differential.

lessons.title: No separate visible sinus P
lessons.explanation: No distinct sinus P wave is visible in this teaching example. P may be buried or retrograde; this alone cannot identify the circuit.

name: Junctional escape rhythm
summary: A regular narrow-complex escape rhythm at 40/min with no visible preceding P wave. Retrograde P waves may have different positions in real tracings.

lessons.title: Slow narrow escape
lessons.explanation: The modeled ventricular interval is 1.5 seconds, corresponding to 40/min.

lessons.title: No preceding sinus P
lessons.explanation: Inspect the baseline before QRS: no distinct sinus P is drawn. A complete ECG and clinical assessment are required.

name: First-degree AV block
summary: Every P conducts, but the PR is prolonged to 280 ms. This is AV conduction delay without dropped ventricular beats.

lessons.title: Prolonged PR
lessons.explanation: Measure from P onset to QRS onset: this model uses 280 ms, above the adult 200 ms threshold.

lessons.title: One P for each QRS
lessons.explanation: Each regular atrial impulse is followed by a QRS. No impulses are dropped in first-degree AV block.

name: Mobitz I · Wenckebach
summary: Progressive PR prolongation culminates in a nonconducted P wave, then the sequence resets.

lessons.title: PR progressively lengthens
lessons.explanation: The conducted PR intervals are 160, 220 and 280 ms in this repeating group.

lessons.title: P wave without QRS
lessons.explanation: The fourth P wave is not followed by a ventricular complex.

lessons.title: PR resets after the pause
lessons.explanation: The next conducted beat returns to the shortest PR of 160 ms.

name: Mobitz II AV block
summary: An on-time P wave suddenly fails to conduct while the PR intervals before and after it remain constant.

lessons.title: Constant conducted PR
lessons.explanation: Conducted beats have the same 180 ms PR, without progressive lengthening.

lessons.title: Abrupt dropped QRS
lessons.explanation: The fourth P wave occurs on schedule but has no following QRS. The atrial cycle remains constant.

lessons.title: PR unchanged after the block
lessons.explanation: The next conducted beat has the same PR as those before the dropped beat. Exclude mimics such as blocked atrial ectopy.

name: 2:1 AV block
summary: Every alternate P wave is nonconducted. A 2:1 strip alone cannot reliably classify Mobitz I versus Mobitz II.

lessons.title: Two P waves for each QRS
lessons.explanation: Atrial activity continues at 75/min while ventricular complexes occur at about 37.5/min.

lessons.title: Alternate P is blocked
lessons.explanation: Inspect the isolated P between two conducted beats; it is not followed by QRS.

lessons.title: Do not force a Mobitz label
lessons.explanation: Only one conducted PR is seen per pair, so progressive PR behavior cannot be assessed from this pattern alone.

name: Right bundle branch block
summary: Focused V1 and V6 views illustrate a broad QRS, terminal R′ in V1 and a broad terminal S in V6.

lessons.title: Broad rSR′ in V1
lessons.explanation: The QRS is 150 ms with a terminal positive R′ in the right precordial view.

lessons.title: Broad terminal S in V6
lessons.explanation: The lateral view has a widened terminal negative deflection. Read the lead views together.

lessons.title: Secondary repolarization
lessons.explanation: The terminal T direction opposes the late QRS direction in the right precordial example.

name: Left bundle branch block
summary: Focused V1 and V6 views illustrate a broad predominantly negative right-precordial QRS and broad notched lateral R.

lessons.title: Broad negative QRS in V1
lessons.explanation: The QRS is 160 ms and predominantly negative in this right precordial lead.

lessons.title: Broad notched R in V6
lessons.explanation: The lateral QRS is broad and positive, with no initial septal q in this modeled view.

lessons.title: Discordant ST–T direction
lessons.explanation: Repolarization opposes the major QRS direction. New LBBB alone does not establish acute coronary occlusion.

name: Prolonged QT
summary: At 60/min, this example has QT 540 ms; the rate-corrected value is also 540 ms. The tracing does not distinguish acquired from congenital causes.

lessons.title: QT to the end of T
lessons.explanation: Measure from QRS onset at 500 ms to T end at 1,040 ms. A separate U wave would not be included.

lessons.title: Rate correction matters
lessons.explanation: The R–R is 1,000 ms here, so QT and QTc coincide. At other rates the correction formula affects interpretation.

lessons.title: Assess reversible causes
lessons.explanation: Review medications, electrolytes and prior ECGs. QT prolongation raises concern for torsades risk but does not predict an individual event.

name: Premature ventricular complex
summary: An early broad ventricular complex interrupts sinus rhythm and is followed by a full compensatory pause in this example.

lessons.title: Early broad complex
lessons.explanation: The ectopic QRS arrives at 1,900 ms, earlier than the expected sinus beat at 2,100 ms; it is broad and has a different shape.

lessons.title: No preceding conducted P
lessons.explanation: No P wave is drawn immediately before the ectopic complex. The ventricular morphology differs from the sinus complexes.

lessons.title: Compensatory pause
lessons.explanation: The normal QRS before the PVC and the next normal QRS are 1,600 ms apart, twice the baseline 800 ms cycle.

name: Premature atrial complex
summary: An early atrial depolarization with a different P shape conducts through a narrow QRS and resets the rhythm.

lessons.title: Premature altered P
lessons.explanation: The early atrial wave before the 1,900 ms QRS has a different polarity in this example.

lessons.title: Narrow conducted QRS
lessons.explanation: The premature atrial impulse conducts with the same narrow ventricular morphology as the sinus beats.

lessons.title: Noncompensatory pause
lessons.explanation: The normal beats on either side are less than two baseline cycles apart because the atrial ectopy resets timing.

name: Ventricular paced rhythm
summary: Pacing stimuli precede broad ventricular complexes. Electrical capture is illustrated; mechanical capture requires clinical assessment.

lessons.title: Pacing stimulus
lessons.explanation: A narrow vertical stimulus precedes each QRS. Modern bipolar pacing spikes can be subtle on a real ECG.

lessons.title: Electrical capture
lessons.explanation: Each stimulus is followed by a broad complex in this example. Check every spike rather than assuming capture.

lessons.title: Secondary ST–T changes
lessons.explanation: The repolarization direction opposes the broad QRS. A paced ECG still requires ischemia assessment in the appropriate setting.

name: Ventricular fibrillation
summary: Disorganized ventricular activity with no repeating organized QRS. Assess the patient immediately and distinguish artifact.

lessons.title: Disorganized waveform
lessons.explanation: The amplitude, contour and interval vary without a repeating P–QRS–T sequence.

lessons.title: No organized QRS train
lessons.explanation: There are no consistently identifiable ventricular complexes to count as a perfusing rhythm.

lessons.title: Clinical arrest assessment
lessons.explanation: In an unresponsive patient without a pulse, VF is a shockable arrest rhythm. ECG appearance must be correlated with the patient.

name: Torsades de pointes pattern
summary: Prolonged QT in the initial sinus beats precedes a polymorphic ventricular run with waxing and waning amplitude.

lessons.title: Prolonged QT before the run
lessons.explanation: The initial sinus beats have QT 540 ms at 60/min. Torsades is polymorphic VT associated with prolonged QT, not every polymorphic VT.

lessons.title: Changing polarity and amplitude
lessons.explanation: The ventricular run changes direction and amplitude around the baseline. This is an illustrative rhythm strip.

lessons.title: No stable complexes for synchronization
lessons.explanation: Sustained polymorphic VT requires immediate unsynchronized shock under AHA guidance. Do not delay shock while attempting synchronization.

name: Asystole · verify the recording
summary: No discernible ventricular electrical activity is illustrated. Confirm the patient, electrodes, leads and gain before labeling asystole.

lessons.title: No ventricular complexes
lessons.explanation: There is no organized ventricular activity in this idealized recording.

lessons.title: Exclude technical causes and fine VF
lessons.explanation: Check another lead, electrode contact and gain; a flat line can also reflect a disconnected system.

lessons.title: Nonshockable arrest rhythm
lessons.explanation: When cardiac arrest with asystole is confirmed, follow the nonshockable arrest pathway. Defibrillation does not treat asystole.

name: Pulseless electrical activity · clinical case
summary: Organized electrical activity without a palpable pulse is PEA. There is no unique ECG shape that diagnoses PEA.

lessons.title: Organized electrical activity
lessons.explanation: The strip contains repeating narrow ventricular complexes. Their presence does not establish mechanical circulation.

lessons.title: The absent pulse defines this case
lessons.explanation: The supplied clinical scenario, not the waveform alone, makes this PEA. The same electrical tracing could occur with a pulse.

lessons.title: Nonshockable arrest pathway
lessons.explanation: Confirmed PEA requires the nonshockable pathway and a search for reversible causes. Reassess the rhythm as care continues.

stem: Clinical scenario: the patient is unresponsive, is not breathing normally, and has no palpable pulse.

name: Hyperacute T-wave comparison
summary: Compare normal, broad hyperacute and narrow peaked T morphology. Distribution, symptoms and serial change remain essential.

name: Modified Sgarbossa patterns
summary: Concordant and excessive discordant ST changes support occlusion assessment in LBBB or ventricular pacing.

name: Posterior occlusion pattern
summary: Anterior mirror changes are compared with the complete V7–V9 posterior set. Interpret supplemental-lead elevation with age-specific thresholds and the clinical context.

name: Diffuse ST depression with aVR elevation
summary: A global ischemia pattern that does not identify a specific coronary lesion. Consider ACS and supply–demand causes.

lessons.title: Widespread ST depression
lessons.explanation: Horizontal ST depression is present in the displayed limb and lateral chest leads. Assess the distribution on a complete ECG and compare serial changes.

lessons.title: Opposite aVR elevation
lessons.explanation: The aVR ST segment is elevated while several other leads are depressed. This indicates global subendocardial ischemia in context; it cannot identify a left-main lesion.

lessons.title: Interpret perfusion and symptoms
lessons.explanation: Consider ACS as well as severe supply–demand imbalance. Ongoing ischemia or hemodynamic compromise needs urgent assessment; this pattern is not an automatic STEMI diagnosis.

name: Hyperkalemia · three appearances
summary: Peaked T, conduction slowing and sine-wave appearances are alternatives, not a predictable sequence or potassium-level scale.

name: Hypokalemia pattern
summary: Small T waves, ST depression and prominent separate U waves are illustrated. Confirm potassium with laboratory testing.

lessons.title: Depressed ST and flattened T
lessons.explanation: The ST lies below the TP baseline and the T wave is small. ECG appearances cannot determine the potassium concentration or exclude hypokalemia.

lessons.title: U follows the completed T
lessons.explanation: A separate positive U follows T. This model ends T at 380 ms and U at 620 ms after QRS onset; U must not be counted as part of QT.

lessons.title: QT versus QU
lessons.explanation: Measure QRS onset to T end, not to U end. When T and U merge clinically, use another lead with a clear endpoint rather than reporting a falsely precise QT.

name: Hypothermia · J wave
summary: A J hump follows QRS. The ECG alone cannot establish body temperature or the cause of a J wave.

lessons.title: Sinus bradycardia at 40/min
lessons.explanation: Each QRS is preceded by P; the R–R interval is 1,500 ms. Hypothermia may also cause atrial fibrillation and other arrhythmias.

lessons.title: J wave at the QRS–ST junction
lessons.explanation: A rounded Osborn hump follows the terminal QRS. J waves are compatible with hypothermia but are not specific for it and do not measure core temperature.

lessons.title: Prolonged conduction and repolarization
lessons.explanation: This model has PR 240 ms, QRS 120 ms and QT 560 ms. QT is the uncorrected interval; evaluate core temperature and the patient.

name: Sodium-channel blockade pattern
summary: Broad QRS and terminal R in aVR are clues in a compatible toxic exposure; assess the clinical context.

lessons.title: QRS widening
lessons.explanation: The modeled QRS lasts 160 ms. Sodium-channel blocker poisoning is one possible cause of a broad QRS; compare the exposure history and prior ECG.

lessons.title: Prominent terminal R in aVR
lessons.explanation: The last positive aVR deflection is 4 mm, following a 5 mm S wave (R/S 0.8). A terminal R of at least 3 mm or R/S greater than 0.7 supports this toxic pattern in context.

lessons.title: Do not diagnose poisoning from aVR alone
lessons.explanation: A terminal aVR R can have other causes. In suspected life-threatening sodium-channel blocker poisoning, urgent toxicology-directed care includes sodium bicarbonate with monitored endpoints.

name: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
summary: Wide ventricular tachycardia with modeled AV dissociation, capture and fusion beats. These features may be absent in real VT.

name: Complete AV block
summary: Independent atrial activity continues while a slower ventricular escape rhythm provides ventricular activation.

name: Ventricular pre-excitation · WPW pattern
summary: Short PR and delta upstroke illustrate sinus pre-excitation. This is not a tracing of pre-excited atrial fibrillation.

lessons.title: Short PR to delta onset
lessons.explanation: P onset to the first ventricular deflection is 100 ms. Measure PR to the start of the delta wave, not to the steep R upstroke.

lessons.title: Delta wave and broad QRS
lessons.explanation: The first 40 ms of ventricular activation is slurred; the entire QRS lasts 140 ms. Degree and polarity of pre-excitation vary by lead and accessory pathway.

lessons.title: Sinus pattern versus pre-excited AF
lessons.explanation: This regular rhythm has organized P waves. WPW pattern does not by itself establish symptomatic WPW syndrome. The separate pre-excited AF example shows a very different irregular tachycardia.

name: Brugada type 1 pattern
summary: Coved right-precordial ST elevation followed by T inversion requires proper lead placement and exclusion of phenocopies.

lessons.title: Coved right-precordial elevation
lessons.explanation: The J/ST junction is elevated 3 mm in V1 and 2.5 mm in V2 at standard gain, descending in a coved contour. Type 1 morphology requires at least 2 mm in at least one of V1 or V2.

lessons.title: Negative T after the cove
lessons.explanation: Follow the elevated ST continuously into an inverted T wave. A saddleback appearance alone is not the diagnostic type 1 pattern.

lessons.title: Pattern versus syndrome
lessons.explanation: Use V1/V2 in the second, third or fourth intercostal spaces when clinically indicated. Assess fever, drugs, symptoms, family history and phenocopies; this synthetic pattern alone does not establish Brugada syndrome.

name: Right ventricular strain pattern
summary: S1Q3T3 and anterior T inversion are strain clues, neither diagnostic nor sufficiently sensitive to exclude pulmonary embolism.

lessons.title: Sinus tachycardia
lessons.explanation: The sinus rate is 110/min with a P before each QRS. Tachycardia is common in PE but highly nonspecific.

lessons.title: S in I; Q and inverted T in III
lessons.explanation: Read the deep terminal S in I with the initial Q and negative T in III. S1Q3T3 is a right-heart strain clue, not a diagnosis of PE.

lessons.title: Anterior T-wave inversion
lessons.explanation: Negative T waves in V1–V4 support right ventricular strain in context. Similar changes have other causes; a normal ECG cannot exclude PE.

name: Pericarditis pattern
summary: PR depression and ST elevation are illustrated in selected leads. Concavity alone cannot distinguish pericarditis from coronary occlusion.

lessons.title: ST elevation across lead territories
lessons.explanation: The displayed limb and lateral chest leads have upward-concave ST elevation. Confirm widespread involvement on the full ECG; concavity alone cannot exclude coronary occlusion.

lessons.title: PR depression relative to TP
lessons.explanation: The PR segment is below the TP baseline in the positive leads. Compare a true TP baseline rather than using the displaced PR as zero.

lessons.title: Opposite aVR PR and ST changes
lessons.explanation: aVR has PR elevation and ST depression. ECG findings support pericarditis only with the history and other diagnostic evidence; use the separate early-repolarization case for comparison.

name: Electrical alternans
summary: Repeating changes in QRS amplitude are illustrated. This finding alone does not diagnose tamponade.

lessons.title: Alternating QRS amplitude
lessons.explanation: Successive QRS complexes alternate between larger and smaller amplitudes while their timing remains regular. Assess several cycles to distinguish alternans from artifact or ectopy.

lessons.title: Sinus tachycardia at 110/min
lessons.explanation: A P precedes each QRS and the R–R interval is about 545 ms. P and T amplitudes also alternate in this model.

lessons.title: Small voltage is not a complete low-voltage diagnosis
lessons.explanation: These selected leads have small complexes. Formal low voltage requires assessment of every lead in the relevant limb or precordial set. Alternans does not prove tamponade; assess the patient and obtain echocardiography when indicated.

name: LVH voltage and low-voltage comparison
summary: Compare high-voltage and low-voltage examples. Voltage criteria alone do not establish anatomic hypertrophy.

name: Pre-excited atrial fibrillation
summary: Very rapid irregular ventricular activity with changing QRS width and morphology, without organized P waves.

lessons.title: Rapid irregular R–R intervals
lessons.explanation: The ventricular intervals vary from 220 to 390 ms. The shortest modeled interval is below 250 ms, a high-risk clue in pre-excited AF.

lessons.title: Changing broad QRS complexes
lessons.explanation: QRS width, amplitude and contour vary with the modeled degree of pre-excitation. There are no organized P waves. An irregular wide tachycardia requires urgent assessment.

lessons.title: Recognize the treatment distinction
lessons.explanation: In pre-excited AF, AV-nodal blockers including adenosine, beta blockers, verapamil/diltiazem, digoxin and IV amiodarone can be harmful. Instability requires immediate electrical cardioversion; stable treatment requires an appropriate monitored pathway.

name: Early repolarization pattern
summary: Selected inferolateral leads show J notching and upward-concave ST elevation. This appearance alone does not establish a benign cause of chest pain.

lessons.title: Terminal QRS notch
lessons.explanation: A notch appears at the QRS–ST junction with J elevation in the displayed inferolateral leads. Distinguish it from a separate pacing spike or artifact.

lessons.title: Concave ST with upright T
lessons.explanation: The ST rises toward an upright T wave, with no PR depression in this model. Neither concavity nor notching alone excludes acute ischemia.

lessons.title: Compare symptoms and prior ECGs
lessons.explanation: A stable prior pattern supports early repolarization, but new symptoms still require clinical assessment and serial ECGs when indicated. Compare with the pericarditis and territorial STEMI examples.

name: Hypocalcemia · prolonged ST/QT
summary: Prolonged ST duration produces a long QT in this example; confirm calcium and consider other causes of QT prolongation.

lessons.title: ST duration changes QT
lessons.explanation: At 60/min, QRS onset to T end is 540 ms; the ST segment is prolonged. The separate long-QT case illustrates a different T/ST contour.

lessons.title: Confirm the cause clinically
lessons.explanation: The ECG cannot determine a calcium concentration. Review laboratory measurements, medications and other acquired or congenital causes of the interval change.

name: Hypercalcemia · short ST/QT
summary: A short ST segment produces a short QT in this example; confirm calcium and consider other causes of short QT.

lessons.title: ST duration changes QT
lessons.explanation: At 60/min, QRS onset to T end is 280 ms, with a very short ST segment. QT and QTc coincide at this rate.

lessons.title: Confirm the cause clinically
lessons.explanation: The ECG cannot determine a calcium concentration. Review laboratory measurements, medications and other acquired or congenital causes of the interval change.
